title: row20
live_proof: inspection with line numbers in the 3.22.0 tree: blobReadWrite() calls sqlite3BtreeIntegerKey() at vdbeblob.c:420 with no cursor-valid check, and the preupdate hook runs with that key at :421. Fixed upstream in 3.51.0 by reseeking first and skipping the hook if it cannot restore
object: the btree page the blob cursor was parked on
lifetime_ender: another writer modifies or deletes the row, so the cursor is saved and the page released, but pCur->pPage is left set
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Needs -DSQLITE_ENABLE_PREUPDATE_HOOK, without which the second half of the sequence does not exist

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting -- SIGPROT(34) with si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is recorded as a catch by the same rule the virtual arms use, and the note says what actually cleared the tag. A fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect

note: WITHDRAWN by the case-by-case review of 2026-10-17, and the REASON MADE PRECISE on 2026-10-20: its trigger reaches the defect's CONDITION and performs no invalid memory access, which is what this case's own evidence below establishes. An earlier revision of this note said the trigger "does not reach the defect it names", which understated what was measured: the cursor is exactly in the state upstream 8504d37b99 describes, and what follows is a stale KEY handed to the preupdate hook -- a correctness defect, not a memory access. The lifetime that ended is the cursor's reference to the page, which is neither freed nor reassigned, so no memory-safety mechanism can see it by construction. The directory and its number are kept so that every record written against them stays resolvable, and so that the silicon and vp2 arms, whose bundles are keyed to this numbering, are not broken. It is out of the corpus's denominator; see README.md. || Trigger reaches the bug CONDITION but makes no invalid access (2026-10-11, gdb on the host -O0 build). At vdbeblob.c:420 the cursor is exactly as upstream 8504d37b99 describes: eState=CURSOR_REQUIRESEEK, iPage=-1, and the saved page unpinned in the cache (pPage->pDbPage->nRef=0). No stale read follows, because info.nSize=69 is still set, so getCellInfo returns the cursor's cached cell info instead of parsing the unpinned page; the preupdate hook therefore receives a stale key, which is a correctness defect, not a memory access. The btreeParseCellPtr seen on that same page afterwards comes from accessPayload once the restore has re-pinned it (nRef=1). The lifetime that ended here is the CURSOR'S REFERENCE to the page, which btreeReleaseAllCursorPages dropped while pCur->pPage stayed set: the page is neither freed nor reassigned, so ASan cannot see it by construction. RETRACTED the same day: this note first said a per-reference lifetime at the pager would express it. Measured, that breaks the engine -- pcacheUnpin is a no-op for an in-memory database and SQLite reads page data at nRef==0, so revoking when the reference count reaches zero faults every in-memory case of this corpus in sqlite3Get4byte while reading page 1's header. The boundary a lifetime CAN express is the page RECYCLE, which sublet/sublet-3220000-pagecache.patch covers; this trigger reaches only the unpin, which that patch deliberately leaves alone.
